questions.stem: The locus of points equidistant from two intersecting lines is:

options.text: The perpendicular bisector of the lines
The pair of angle bisectors of the lines
A single straight line parallel to both

questions.explanation: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the angle bisectors. Since two lines form two pairs of vertically opposite angles, there are two perpendicular angle bisectors.

questions.stem: A dog is tied to a post by a rope of length $4\text{ m}$. What shape describes the region the dog can reach?
questions.explanation: The dog can move in any direction up to $4\text{ m}$ from the post, so the reachable region is a circle with radius $4\text{ m}$ centred on the post.

questions.stem: The locus of points that are exactly $3\text{ cm}$ from a straight line is:

options.text: A single line parallel to it, $3\text{ cm}$ away
Two parallel lines, one on each side, each $3\text{ cm}$ from the original line

questions.explanation: Points exactly $3\text{ cm}$ from a straight line lie on two parallel lines, one on each side of the original line, each at a perpendicular distance of $3\text{ cm}$.
